# Proof

**Claim:** Yes, $Z(G)/N = Z(G/N)$.

## Step 1: $N \subseteq Z(G)$

Since $N$ is normal in $G$, for any $n \in N$ the map
$$\phi_n : G \to N, \quad \phi_n(g) = gng^{-1}$$
is well-defined and continuous (composition of multiplication and inversion, all continuous). Since $G$ is connected, $\phi_n(G)$ is a connected subset of $N$. But $N$ is discrete, so its only connected subsets are singletons. Since $\phi_n(e) = n$, we get $\phi_n(g) = n$ for all $g \in G$, i.e., $n \in Z(G)$. Hence $N \subseteq Z(G)$.

## Step 2: $Z(G)/N \subseteq Z(G/N)$

Let $\pi : G \to G/N$ be the quotient map. For $z \in Z(G)$ and any $h \in G$,
$$\pi(z)\pi(h) = \pi(zh) = \pi(hz) = \pi(h)\pi(z),$$
so $\pi(z) \in Z(G/N)$. Thus $\pi(Z(G)) = Z(G)/N \subseteq Z(G/N)$.

## Step 3: $Z(G/N) \subseteq Z(G)/N$

Suppose $g \in G$ with $\pi(g) \in Z(G/N)$. Then for every $h \in G$,
$$\pi(ghg^{-1}h^{-1}) = \pi(g)\pi(h)\pi(g)^{-1}\pi(h)^{-1} = e_{G/N},$$
so the commutator $[g,h] := ghg^{-1}h^{-1} \in N$ for all $h \in G$.

Consider the map
$$\psi : G \to N, \quad \psi(h) = [g,h] = ghg^{-1}h^{-1}.$$
This is continuous (product of continuous maps $h \mapsto g$, $h \mapsto h$, $h \mapsto g^{-1}$, $h \mapsto h^{-1}$ followed by group multiplication). Since $G$ is connected, $\psi(G)$ is connected. Since $N$ is discrete, $\psi(G)$ is a single point. Since $\psi(e) = e$, we conclude $\psi(h) = e$ for all $h \in G$, i.e., $gh = hg$ for all $h$. Hence $g \in Z(G)$.

Therefore $\pi(g) \in Z(G)/N$, giving $Z(G/N) \subseteq Z(G)/N$.

## Conclusion

Combining Steps 2 and 3, $Z(G)/N = Z(G/N)$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE

But $N$ is discrete, so its only connected subsets are singletons. Since $\phi_n(e) = n$, we get $\phi_n(g) = n$ for all $g \in G$, i.e., $n \in Z(G)$. Hence $N \subseteq Z(G)$.

## Step 2: $Z(G)/N \subseteq Z(G/N)$

Let $\pi : G \to G/N$ be the quotient map. For $z \in Z(G)$ and any $h \in G$,
$$\pi(z)\pi(h) = \pi(zh) = \pi(hz) = \pi(h)\pi(z),$$
so $\pi(z) \in Z(G/N)$. Thus $\pi(Z(G)) = Z(G)/N \subseteq Z(G/N)$.

## Step 3: $Z(G/N) \subseteq Z(G)/N$

Suppose $g \in G$ with $\pi(g) \in Z(G/N)$. Then for every $h \in G$,
$$\pi(ghg^{-1}h^{-1}) = \pi(g)\pi(h)\pi(g)^{-1}\pi(h)^{-1} = e_{G/N},$$
so the commutator $[g,h] := ghg^{-1}h^{-1} \in N$ for all $h \in G$.

Consider the map
$$\psi : G \to N, \quad \psi(h) = [g,h] = ghg^{-1}h^{-1}.$$
This is continuous (product of continuous maps $h \mapsto g$, $h \mapsto h$, $h \mapsto g^{-1}$, $h \mapsto h^{-1}$ followed by group multiplication). Since $G$ is connected, $\psi(G)$ is connected. Since $N$ is discrete, $\psi(G)$ is a single point. Since $\psi(e) = e$, we conclude $\psi(h) = e$ for all $h \in G$, i.e., $gh = hg$ for all $h$. Hence $g \in Z(G)$.

Therefore $\pi(g) \in Z(G)/N$, giving $Z(G/N) \subseteq Z(G)/N$.
